data.name: Akash
data.gender_notes: Akash is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Akash is the deity representing the sky and the infinite space. It is the first element in the universe and the birthplace of all atoms. Akash is also associated with the breath of life and the ethereal plane, where the soul resides. The name Akash carries the meaning “Sky, Space, Cosmos” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Akash usually hope their child will grow to embody sky, space, cosmos and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes boundless knowledge, freedom, and the infinite nature of the universe.
data.etymology: Akash belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sky, Space, Cosmos.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Akash total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Akash has its origins in Hindu mythology, where it is the name of the god representing the sky and infinite space. In Indian cultures, names are considered important, and Akash is seen as a powerful and unique name. In Hindu scriptures and Vedic texts, Akash is often referred to as the first element in the universe and the birthplace of all atoms. It symbolizes the sky as a vast canvas of possibilities and the infinite expanse of life.
data.spiritual_significance: Akash holds a significant spiritual meaning as it is believed to be the abode of the soul and the ethereal plane. The word Akash also means "space" or "sky," which can be interpreted as the vast expanse of existence and the limitless potential of the universe. In spiritual practices and meditation, one can visualize the soul (Atman) as a spark of light in the infinite Akash, reminding us of our connection to the divine and the limitless nature of creation. The breath of life, which sustains us physically, is also a reminder of the spiritual breath that sustains our soul in the infinite space of Akash.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Akash symbolizes the infinite and boundless sky, representing the purest form of consciousness and the cosmic expanse. It is the silent witness of all creation, the unmanifested reality behind the manifest world.

vedic_reference.note: Akash is a primordial deity mentioned in various Hindu scriptures. In the Rigveda, Akash is considered the first element of the five basic elements (Panchamahabhootas).

historical_references.reference: Akash is the Sanskrit word for 'sky' or 'space'. It is mentioned in various Hindu texts, including the Vedas and the Upanishads.
historical_references.context: Akash is a significant concept in Hinduism, representing the infinite, unchanging, and all-encompassing reality.

trends: Akash is a popular name for boys in India and Nepal
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Akash remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Anita Akash in Chennai, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Akash, which means "Sky, Space, Cosmos". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
